obligations.seam: device update agent ↔ OSTree remote (over Tailscale)
obligations.behavior: Pull+deploy is atomic: interrupted download or power loss leaves the current deployment booted and unchanged
obligations.source_text: OTA uses OSTree via meta-updater: meta-qcom-distro's qcom-distro-sota distro (conf/distro/qcom-distro-sota.conf, ci/qcom-distro-sota.yml) is the only update framework shipped by the Qualcomm layers — no RAUC/SWUpdate/Mender found — giving atomic rootfs deployments with rollback

obligations.behavior: A deployment that fails its boot health check is abandoned and the previous one boots automatically, no hands-on step
obligations.source_text: OTA: one update deployed over Tailscale reboots into the new OSTree deployment, and a deliberately broken deployment rolls back to the previous one within 1 reboot cycle without hands-on access

obligations.behavior: Unsigned or wrongly-signed commits are rejected before deploy, with a logged reason
obligations.source_text: OTA updates are signed and the device refuses unsigned or wrongly-signed OSTree commits; updates are pulled only over Tailscale; sshd allows key auth only (no passwords, no root login)

obligations.behavior: No OTA payload writes MCU firmware; the /var/run/arduino-router.sock API is unchanged across OS updates
obligations.source_text: MCU stays out of the OS image path: STM32H5 runs Zephyr, Linux talks to it via arduino-router on /dev/ttyACM0 (+ /var/run/arduino-router.sock); CultureOS must preserve or package arduino-router and never flash MCU firmware as part of OTA (issue #3 MCU boundary)

obligations.behavior: arduino-router starts at boot and owns /dev/ttyACM0; nothing else opens it
obligations.source_text: The CultureOS image packages arduino-router (static aarch64 Go binary from the 'arduino-router' deb on the factory OS; source github.com/arduino/arduino-router) so Linux can still reach the STM32 MCU over /dev/ttyACM0 after leaving Ubuntu

obligations.behavior: Wi-Fi/SSH secrets are read from an operator-supplied provisioning input at first boot and stored only under /var — never present in the image or repo
obligations.source_text: Connectivity survives the reflash: the CultureOS image restores Wi-Fi (bar-nachum_EXT, credentials provisioned at first boot, never committed), installs Tailscale (operator runs tailscale up once, per q2), and ships the operator's SSH public key for user arduino

obligations.behavior: Tailnet identity (name cultureos, 100.x IP) survives reboot, OTA and rollback without re-auth
obligations.source_text: The board joins the tailnet (Tailscale) so it is reachable for management and OTA from anywhere, not just the home LAN — the DGX Spark is already on it (tailscale0 100.127.105.72)

obligations.behavior: Node starts after network-online, restarts on crash, keeps its mesh identity under /var across OTA
obligations.source_text: The updated image boots into a supervised Culture mesh node (culture installs via 'uv tool install culture' + 'culture server start', culture/README.md:73-74) so the board is reachable on the mesh after every OTA (issue #3 M2)

obligations.behavior: Reports deployed version + last update outcome (applied/rolled-back/failed) with --json, exit 0 healthy / non-zero degraded
obligations.source_text: The board reports its deployed OS version and the outcome of the last update (applied / rolled back / failed) somewhere the operator sees without SSH — e.g. a cultureos doctor/status verb and the Culture mesh

obligations.behavior: A shell is reachable with networking down (no Ethernet, no Wi-Fi)
obligations.source_text: The image keeps a local access path that does not depend on the network: USB gadget (adbd and/or CDC-ACM serial — the factory OS exposes /dev/ttyGS0 via arduino-router-serial) or the UART console ttyMSM0 (on the factory kernel cmdline), so a broken network config is recoverable without EDL

obligations.behavior: Installing or updating CultureOS never modifies eMMC partitions; factory Ubuntu remains bootable
obligations.source_text: The CultureOS OS (ESP-chainloaded kernel + OSTree sysroot) lives on NVMe; the eMMC keeps the boot firmware (_a/_b, untouched) and, if UEFI can boot NVMe, the factory Ubuntu as an always-available fallback OS — so a bad CultureOS install never bricks the board

obligations.behavior: Every published image bundle includes LICENSE.qcom-2 and ships firmware in binary form only
obligations.source_text: Published image artifacts carry Qualcomm's LICENSE.qcom-2 text: the QCS8300 boot binaries are redistributable only in binary form, only for Qualcomm chips, and must include the license (meta-qcom/licenses/LICENSE.qcom-2 §1.1-1.2; firmware-qcom-boot-qcs8300.inc)

obligations.seam: culture-rules release workflow ↔ OSTree repo on the Spark
obligations.behavior: Only signed commits from a successful, pinned build are committed; a failed build/sign step leaves the repo's current ref unchanged
obligations.source_text: Releases are driven by a culture-rules rule/workflow: build -> sign -> commit to the OSTree repo -> the board is OTA'd

obligations.behavior: The upgrade trigger is idempotent and reports the board's resulting deployment (applied/rolled-back) back into the run record
obligations.source_text: Releases are driven by a culture-rules rule/workflow: build -> sign -> commit to the OSTree repo -> the board is OTA'd

obligations.behavior: A new deployment becomes default only after its health check passes; any reset before that boots the previous default
obligations.source_text: Rollback strategy (proposed for q5): keep upstream systemd-boot; each new OSTree deployment is staged non-default and booted once via LoaderEntryOneShot (trial boot); qcom_wdt armed early (systemd RuntimeWatchdogSec) + kernel panic reboot turn any panic/hang into a reset that lands on the old default; a health-check service promotes the deployment to default only after it passes. Layer 2: an eMMC Ubuntu rescue agent (UEFI BootOrder: NVMe, then eMMC Ubuntu) repairs the NVMe OSTree default when the NVMe OS cannot even load, with a retry cap and alert over Tailscale. Fallback if one-shot misbehaves on this UEFI: GRUB boot counter + greenboot (GRUB EFI proven on this board)

obligations.behavior: Watchdog is armed by early boot and a userspace or kernel hang resets the board within the watchdog timeout
